title: compliance-report
description: One report of the compliance officer (roles/compliance-officer.json): one agent, one finding, seen on its screen. One report per seat per finding, never repeated; `key` is that pair and the consumer drops a second report with the same key. $defs.finding_codes is the closed finding-code map: code, meaning, who acts, and the event code the report is carried with. The officer reports; it never nudges, fixes or stops anyone, so the one who acts is always another seat or the owner. The patrol is a one-minute tick: a hung seat or a dead process is reported within one tick.

reporter.description: the seat that wrote the report

seat.description: the watched agent the finding is about, the architect and the orchestrator included; for a process finding the process slug (belt, flow, lease, bearings)

ticket.description: the ticket that seat holds, null for a seat that holds none

pane.description: the herdr pane id of the watched agent; null for a process finding that has no pane

finding.description: a code from $defs.finding_codes; the list is closed, so an unknown code is invalid

code.description: the event status code every report is carried with; the finding is the discriminator, not the number

acts.description: who acts on the finding, copied from $defs.finding_codes; the officer never acts. Findings go to the orchestrator lane; a process finding goes to the maintenance worker's lane

seen.description: what was seen on the screen, one line

evidence.description: lines quoted from the watched agent's screen, colons replaced by spaces

first_seen.description: UTC, ISO 8601, Z suffix: the first patrol that saw the finding

last_seen.description: UTC, ISO 8601, Z suffix: the patrol that wrote this report

finding_codes.description: The closed finding-code map. Keys equal the `finding` enum above (a test asserts it). `acts` follows the chain owner, architect, orchestrator, system: a worker, tester, reviewer, merger, monitor or player is answered to by the orchestrator, the orchestrator by the architect, the architect by the owner. A law broken by the architect or the orchestrator has its own code so the finding is never lost in a worker bucket. The maintenance worker is the lane that restarts line processes; it answers to the orchestrator.

CO-WAITING.meaning: an agent is waiting on a question, a menu or an approval prompt that nobody answers

CO-REFUSED.meaning: a tool or command was refused or denied and the agent has not moved on

CO-ERROR-STOPPED.meaning: an agent stopped on an error and is not retrying

CO-IDLE-OWES.meaning: an agent is idle while it owes a record its playbook names

CO-LOOPING.meaning: an agent repeats the same step with the same result

CO-HUNG.meaning: an agent is mid-turn with a busy footer past ten minutes and its last output has not moved

CO-PROC-DEAD.meaning: a line process of the restart runbook is not running (belt, flow, lease, bearings server or wait loop)

CO-PROC-DUPLICATE.meaning: a line process runs more than once at top level; exactly one is allowed

CO-LAW-BACKGROUND.meaning: an agent ran a background job, or a Monitor tool under an agent, against AGENTS.md law herdr-first

CO-LAW-HAND-EDIT.meaning: an agent edited a file outside its allowed paths, or did by hand what the system should do

CO-LAW-OWNER-PROSE.meaning: an agent wrote prose or a question to the owner outside a card on the page

CO-LAW-ARCHITECT.meaning: the architect broke an AGENTS.md law or an owner order, seen on its screen

CO-LAW-ORCHESTRATOR.meaning: the orchestrator broke an AGENTS.md law or an owner order, seen on its screen
